title: LOCAL: out-of-process hop on ONE pinned core costs 4.8 us (UDS) / 2.1 us (futex shm ring) vs 0.02-0.05 us in-process, p50; p99 5.7 us / 2.5 us
summary: Request/response closed loop, client and helper process pinned to one CPU (2 context switches + 4 syscalls per UDS call). Noop op: in-process dyn call 23 ns (timer control 21 ns); UDS+postcard 4796 ns [4750-5899], p99 5706; UDS+bincode 4756; UDS raw length-prefix 4756; shm ring + futex wake 2054 ns [2035-2797], p99 2544; TCP loopback raw 8145 ns [6988-19027]. Echo payload 64B: inproc 24 ns, UDS-postcard 4866 ns, shm 2061 ns. 4KB: inproc 68 ns, UDS-postcard 9804, UDS-raw 5795, shm 2218. 64KB: inproc 1642 ns (memcpy+Vec), UDS-raw 19578 ns (p99 23377), shm 7420 ns (p99 8408), postcard/bincode 96320 ns before serde_bytes fix. Throughput (sequential closed loop, calls/s): inproc noop 21.8M; UDS 214k; shm 465k; 64KB echo UDS-raw 50k, shm 134k. Wasmtime component call reused from r2 (in-process, not IPC): noop 97 ns, 105B handler 1.24 us.
specifics: i9-14900HX, Linux 6.17.0-14-generic, taskset -c 13 (one logical CPU; SMT sibling 12 NOT idle-guaranteed), powersave governor, loadavg 10-23 during runs (other research loops), cpuset /user.slice, rustc 1.88.0 release lto, offline crates: tokio 1.x, bytes 1.x, http 1.x, postcard 1.1.3, bincode 1.3.3, serde_bytes 0.11.19, sha2 0.10, hmac 0.12, libc 0.2. Harness code: state/raw/round-003/02-bench/src, raw data 02-ipc-1core.jsonl (n=10 runs), 02-ipc-2core-control.jsonl (n=5), 02-ipc-1core-tcp.jsonl, 02-ipc-1core-serdebytes.jsonl, 02-rss-1core.jsonl, 02-norm-1core.jsonl. Control: timer floor (Instant pair) 21 ns p50 = no-op control; each run p50/p99 over 10k-20k calls after 300 warm-up; numbers below are medians over 10 runs of per-run p50 (range in brackets). Fixed hop: UDS-postcard-noop minus inproc-noop = 4.77 us; shm-futex = 2.03 us; ratio UDS/shm = 2.3x. Per-byte (raw frame, 4KB->64KB): (19578-5795)/61440 = 0.22 ns/B round-trip, ~4.5 GB/s each way effective incl. 2 copies/dir. Hop share of one core: rate*4.8us = 1k/s 0.5%, 10k/s 4.8%, 50k/s 24%, 100k/s 48%.
overclaim_risk: Measured on a 5.8 GHz-class laptop core under load and powersave governor, not on a KVM 1-vCPU $5 VPS; context-switch cost in a hypervisor guest is typically higher (unmeasured here, see spike). Closed-loop sequential only; no pipelining/batching so it is the worst-case for throughput.
underclaim_risk: Real adapter hops can be amortized by pipelining/batching (not measured); sibling SMT noise inflates p99 and maxes; so the quiet-machine hop may be lower than 4.8 us.

title: NEGATIVE: spin-then-futex shared ring is catastrophic on 1 core (638 us/call, 133x worse than plain futex) and shm+futex is WORSE on 2 cores (4.8 us) than on 1 core (2.1 us)
summary: Spin-5000 (x86 pause ~140 cycles each) before futex_wait on a single pinned CPU: noop 638054 ns p50 [636296-638767], 1.6k calls/s, because the spinner burns its timeslice while the peer cannot run. Same code on 2 CPUs (13,17): 195 ns noop, 160 ns echo64, 283 ns redis-shaped, 1.66 us presign-shaped, 17.1 us 64KB echo, 5.2M calls/s (a real two-core win, 25x lower than 1-core futex). Conversely futex-only with 2 CPUs: 4784 ns vs 2054 ns on one CPU (cross-core wakeup IPI + idle exit); UDS 2 CPUs 8066 ns vs 4796 ns on one.
specifics: i9-14900HX, Linux 6.17.0-14-generic, taskset -c 13 (one logical CPU; SMT sibling 12 NOT idle-guaranteed), powersave governor, loadavg 10-23 during runs (other research loops), cpuset /user.slice, rustc 1.88.0 release lto, offline crates: tokio 1.x, bytes 1.x, http 1.x, postcard 1.1.3, bincode 1.3.3, serde_bytes 0.11.19, sha2 0.10, hmac 0.12, libc 0.2. Harness code: state/raw/round-003/02-bench/src, raw data 02-ipc-1core.jsonl (n=10 runs), 02-ipc-2core-control.jsonl (n=5), 02-ipc-1core-tcp.jsonl, 02-ipc-1core-serdebytes.jsonl, 02-rss-1core.jsonl, 02-norm-1core.jsonl. Control: timer floor (Instant pair) 21 ns p50 = no-op control; each run p50/p99 over 10k-20k calls after 300 warm-up; numbers below are medians over 10 runs of per-run p50 (range in brackets). 2-core control n=5 runs on cpus 13,17 (not SMT siblings).
overclaim_risk: The 5000-iteration spin count was not tuned; a smaller bound would reduce but not remove the 1-core penalty; it is a design negative (do not spin on a 1 vCPU target), not a statement about all spin designs.
underclaim_risk: On >=2 dedicated cores a spin ring gets 160-280 ns hops, i.e. near in-process cost; ignoring that would underclaim shared-memory rings for multi-core hosts.

title: PITFALL: serde default serializes &[u8]/Vec<u8> element-wise; without serde_bytes postcard/bincode make a 64 KB payload hop 4.9x slower (96 us vs 19.6 us)
summary: With #[serde(borrow)] body:&[u8] and no serde_bytes, postcard and bincode 64KB echo took 96.3 / 96.2 us vs raw framing 19.6 us (4KB: 9.8 vs 5.8 us); at 64 B all three formats are equal within 3% (4.87/4.84/4.73 us). After adding #[serde(with="serde_bytes")] the rerun gave postcard 64KB min 19.7 us, 4KB min 5.8 us, matching raw framing (the rerun medians were noisier, 27.4 us and 9.1 us, because host load changed; mins are the clean figures, spread documented in 02-ipc-1core-serdebytes.jsonl). Conclusion: for small control messages the wire format is irrelevant (dominated by 2 context switches); for bodies use bytes fields or pass bodies out-of-band.
specifics: serde_bytes 0.11.19, postcard 1.1.3 (default-features=false, use-std), bincode 1.3.3. i9-14900HX, Linux 6.17.0-14-generic, taskset -c 13 (one logical CPU; SMT sibling 12 NOT idle-guaranteed), powersave governor, loadavg 10-23 during runs (other research loops), cpuset /user.slice, rustc 1.88.0 release lto, offline crates: tokio 1.x, bytes 1.x, http 1.x, postcard 1.1.3, bincode 1.3.3, serde_bytes 0.11.19, sha2 0.10, hmac 0.12, libc 0.2. Harness code: state/raw/round-003/02-bench/src, raw data 02-ipc-1core.jsonl (n=10 runs), 02-ipc-2core-control.jsonl (n=5), 02-ipc-1core-tcp.jsonl, 02-ipc-1core-serdebytes.jsonl, 02-rss-1core.jsonl, 02-norm-1core.jsonl. Control: timer floor (Instant pair) 21 ns p50 = no-op control; each run p50/p99 over 10k-20k calls after 300 warm-up; numbers below are medians over 10 runs of per-run p50 (range in brackets).
overclaim_risk: The 4.9x is specific to the default serde byte-slice path with these crate versions; a custom Serialize or postcard-with-bytes types would not show it.

title: LOCAL: redis-GET-shaped op +4.98 us (UDS) = 100x in-process but ~ one loopback RTT; S3-SigV4-presign-shaped op 1.34 us in-process vs 6.93 us UDS (5.2x) vs 3.46 us shm
summary: redis-GET shape: 17 B key -> 256 B value from a 1024-entry HashMap: inproc 49 ns [44-53]; UDS-postcard 5031 ns (p99 5898); UDS-bincode 4944; UDS-raw 4795; shm-futex 2122; TCP loopback raw 10680 ns median (p50 range 7062-19203). S3 presign shape: 4 HMAC-SHA256 key derivations + SHA-256 of 150 B canonical request + HMAC signature + 363 B URL: inproc 1338 ns [1271-1463]; UDS-postcard 6934 (p99 7806); UDS-raw 6539; shm 3458; TCP 9704. Absolute hop add is constant (4.8-5.6 us) so relative cost depends on the op: pure CPU op of 1.3 us -> 5.2x; a real redis GET over loopback (>= 8.1 us for the bare TCP echo measured here, plus redis work, unmeasured) -> UDS hop adds ~<=50% of just the bare TCP leg and less than the network RTT of any non-loopback store.
specifics: i9-14900HX, Linux 6.17.0-14-generic, taskset -c 13 (one logical CPU; SMT sibling 12 NOT idle-guaranteed), powersave governor, loadavg 10-23 during runs (other research loops), cpuset /user.slice, rustc 1.88.0 release lto, offline crates: tokio 1.x, bytes 1.x, http 1.x, postcard 1.1.3, bincode 1.3.3, serde_bytes 0.11.19, sha2 0.10, hmac 0.12, libc 0.2. Harness code: state/raw/round-003/02-bench/src, raw data 02-ipc-1core.jsonl (n=10 runs), 02-ipc-2core-control.jsonl (n=5), 02-ipc-1core-tcp.jsonl, 02-ipc-1core-serdebytes.jsonl, 02-rss-1core.jsonl, 02-norm-1core.jsonl. Control: timer floor (Instant pair) 21 ns p50 = no-op control; each run p50/p99 over 10k-20k calls after 300 warm-up; numbers below are medians over 10 runs of per-run p50 (range in brackets). Presign uses sha2 0.10 + hmac 0.12 (pure Rust with SHA-NI cpufeatures). No real redis/S3 server was run; the ops are shaped (sizes, compute) not real protocol.
overclaim_risk: Shaped ops are not real Redis RESP or real driver CPU: a real redis-rs/fred client adds protocol parsing, allocation and socket I/O, so the in-process baseline for a true adapter is larger than 49 ns (thus relative overhead smaller than 100x).
underclaim_risk: The adapter that is out-of-process also sits next to a network hop; for remote stores (>=200 us RTT) a 5 us UDS hop is ~2.5%.

title: LOCAL: an idle exec helper costs 2.5 MB RSS / 0.6 MB PSS / 0.56 MB private dirty and 544 us to first reply; fork from a zygote costs 250-615 us depending on zygote heap (1-64 MB)
summary: Minimal helper (771 KB static-ish Rust binary, UDS server blocked on read, one request served): exec: RSS 2488 kB (n=1), 2473 (n=8), 2476 (n=32); Pss 784/618/581 kB; Private_Dirty 560 kB. Fork from zygote: 1 MB heap RSS 2776 kB, PSS 548 kB @32 children, priv 492 kB; 8 MB heap: RSS 9944 kB, PSS 769 kB @32, priv 496 kB; 64 MB heap: RSS 67292 kB, PSS 2511 kB @32 (PSS = shared/N + 0.5 MB), priv 500 kB. Spawn to first reply (n=200): exec 544 us p50 / 841 p99; fork 1MB 250 / 645; 8MB 297 / 511; 64MB 615 / 1060. => marginal private memory of one extra helper ~0.5 MB for a minimal Rust helper; real helpers with rustls/tokio/driver will be larger (unmeasured).
specifics: i9-14900HX, Linux 6.17.0-14-generic, taskset -c 13 (one logical CPU; SMT sibling 12 NOT idle-guaranteed), powersave governor, loadavg 10-23 during runs (other research loops), cpuset /user.slice, rustc 1.88.0 release lto, offline crates: tokio 1.x, bytes 1.x, http 1.x, postcard 1.1.3, bincode 1.3.3, serde_bytes 0.11.19, sha2 0.10, hmac 0.12, libc 0.2. Harness code: state/raw/round-003/02-bench/src, raw data 02-ipc-1core.jsonl (n=10 runs), 02-ipc-2core-control.jsonl (n=5), 02-ipc-1core-tcp.jsonl, 02-ipc-1core-serdebytes.jsonl, 02-rss-1core.jsonl, 02-norm-1core.jsonl. Control: timer floor (Instant pair) 21 ns p50 = no-op control; each run p50/p99 over 10k-20k calls after 300 warm-up; numbers below are medians over 10 runs of per-run p50 (range in brackets). Consistent with r2 07 fork measurements (heap 8MB fork 124 us parent->child first instr; here includes first reply round-trip).
overclaim_risk: Minimal helper; real adapter helper (tokio + rustls + driver) RSS not measured and could be 5-20 MB each. PSS amortization hides that shared pages are charged to the zygote.

title: LOCAL: for a 10 MB streamed body, zero-copy Bytes through http::Request<Body> copies 0 bytes in userspace and uses 30 us user CPU; an owned-decode+encode per-protocol codec copies 20 MB and costs +0.58 ms wall (+28%); a 3-copy variant +0.72 ms (+34%)
summary: Single-thread tokio current_thread pipeline on one pinned CPU: UnixStream pair ingress (64 KB writes) -> core -> UnixStream egress, 10 MB body, n=10. A (BytesMut read_buf, split().freeze(), http::Request<Body> with 8 headers, policy layer sees Bytes, write_all): wall p50 2079 us (min 2069, max 2121), user 30 us, sys 2057 us, allocator bytes 266 KB (30 allocs), explicit userspace copies 0, kernel copies 20.97 MB (read+write). B1 (owned Vec decode + framed encode): wall 2657 us, user 888 us, sys 1779, allocator bytes 21.24 MB, copies 20.97 MB. B2 (decode + native->neutral conversion + encode): wall 2794 us, user 916 us, allocator bytes 31.7 MB, copies 31.46 MB. Memory-only pipeline (16 KB chunks, no sockets): A 349 us (includes common copy #0 into buffer), B1 690 us, B2 738 us; allocation bytes A 68 KB vs 21.0 MB vs 31.5 MB; memcpy 10 MB cold control 548 us. So each extra userspace copy of a streamed body ~ 0.24-0.29 ms per 10 MB (24-29 us/MB); zero-copy saves 22% wall at 1 core on 10 MB bodies and 97% of user CPU; the kernel copy (read+write sys time 2.06 ms) dominates the zero-copy path.
specifics: i9-14900HX, Linux 6.17.0-14-generic, taskset -c 13 (one logical CPU; SMT sibling 12 NOT idle-guaranteed), powersave governor, loadavg 10-23 during runs (other research loops), cpuset /user.slice, rustc 1.88.0 release lto, offline crates: tokio 1.x, bytes 1.x, http 1.x, postcard 1.1.3, bincode 1.3.3, serde_bytes 0.11.19, sha2 0.10, hmac 0.12, libc 0.2. Harness code: state/raw/round-003/02-bench/src, raw data 02-ipc-1core.jsonl (n=10 runs), 02-ipc-2core-control.jsonl (n=5), 02-ipc-1core-tcp.jsonl, 02-ipc-1core-serdebytes.jsonl, 02-rss-1core.jsonl, 02-norm-1core.jsonl. Control: timer floor (Instant pair) 21 ns p50 = no-op control; each run p50/p99 over 10k-20k calls after 300 warm-up; numbers below are medians over 10 runs of per-run p50 (range in brackets). Counting allocator wraps System (alloc/realloc/dealloc), counting enabled only on separate untimed pass; explicit memcpy counter in cp(). bytes 1.12.1 doc: clone/slice O(1) refcount; copy_from_slice copies. http-body 1.1.0 Body::Data: Buf, poll_frame.
overclaim_risk: Variants B1/B2 are constructed strawmen parameterised by copy count; real per-protocol stacks (nginx sendfile/splice, kernel-bypass) can also be zero-copy, so the result bounds the cost of copying, it does not show that any real per-protocol codec copies. Single 10 MB request; small requests (<16 KB) copy in <1 us so the effect vanishes. Not measured: h2/h3 framing (h2 crate copies into frames), TLS (record encryption copies unavoidable).
underclaim_risk: Even a 28-34% wall improvement matters only for large bodies; but the user-CPU 30x gap (30 us vs 888-916 us) is what a CPU-bound 1 vCPU box feels under many concurrent uploads once kernel work is offloaded (splice/sendfile not measured).

title: Prior art: published out-of-process/extension overhead numbers are sparse; best primary figures are MeshInsight (C++ filter +5.7/8.2 us, Wasm no-op +26.3 us, gRPC proxy 5x latency 4x CPU vs TCP) and seL4/Zircon cycle counts
summary: MeshInsight (UW/Duke/Bytedance, arXiv 2207.00592, Jul 2022; pdftotext verified): Envoy HTTP mode, 100 B messages, 30K rps: Fault Injection +5.74 us (3.1%), no-op WebAssembly filter +26.30 us (14.3%); additional overhead of HTTP proxying ~4x latency/3x CPU, gRPC 5x latency/4x CPU vs TCP; sidecar meshes +30-185% latency, +41-92% CPU on benchmark apps. LionsOS (arXiv 2501.06234): seL4 context switch 400-600 cycles; Mi et al. 2019 intra-core fastpath round-trip IPC 986 cycles (seL4) / 2717 (Fiasco) / 8157 (Zircon) - at 3-4 GHz roughly 0.25-0.33 us / 0.7-0.9 us / 2.0-2.7 us, i.e. a verified-microkernel IPC is ~15x cheaper than Linux UDS (4.8 us measured here). Chromium Mojo README: a Mojo call ~1/3 faster with 1/3 fewer context switches than legacy Chrome IPC; ~6 KB heap per bound endpoint; same-process communication should use direct calls. Envoy ext_proc docs (1.37) publish only per-phase latency stat fields (request_header_latency_us etc), no benchmark; OPA-Envoy performance page defines a benchmark method but lists no results; HAProxy SPOE.txt gives no numbers (motivation: blocking client libs); envoy-extproc-sdk README anecdote ~4-5 ms/filter (Python in docker-compose, D). Fuchsia round_trips.cc microbenchmark exists but no published numbers found. Chrome Site Isolation 2018: ~10-13% total memory overhead from more processes (press reports of Google engineer, C).
specifics: Prior-art gap itself is a finding: no primary, reproducible per-call ext_proc/ext_authz/SPOE/Pingora-out-of-process latency exists in the public record I could retrieve (grade: absence-of-evidence, searched 2026-10-25).
overclaim_risk: Different hardware, protocols (gRPC vs UDS) and eras (2019-2022); cycle conversions assume 3-4 GHz and are my arithmetic.
underclaim_risk: Absence of published numbers is not evidence the costs are small; vendor internal numbers may exist.

title: RUSTSEC-2025-0141 (issued 2026-01-07): bincode development ceased permanently; 1.3.3 declared complete; recommended postcard, wincode, bitcode, rkyv
summary: Fetched rustsec.org advisory: reported 2025-12-16, issued 2026-01-07, modified 2026-01-16; no patched versions; alternatives wincode/postcard/bitcode/rkyv. crates.io (queried 2026-10-25): postcard 1.1.3 (2025-07-24), rkyv 0.8.18 (2026-08-05), wincode 0.6.3 (2026-10-13), bincode max_stable 3.0.0 (2025-12-16), iceoryx2 0.10.0 (2026-09-18), shmem-ipc 0.3.0 (2022-11-22). rust_serialization_benchmark (updated 2026-10-05, EPYC 7763 4 vCPU, nightly 2026-10-04) log dataset: postcard 1.1.3 ser 415.6 us / deser 2.34 ms / borrow 628.8 us / 724,953 B; rkyv 0.8.18 ser 251.6 us / deser 1.56-1.92 ms / 1,011,488 B. My hop measurement shows format choice is irrelevant at <=64 B (3% spread), so pick the smaller-TCB, no_std-friendly, maintained one.
specifics: bincode 1.3.3 used only as measurement control; do not pin in product.
overclaim_risk: Advisory is unmaintained-class, not a vulnerability.

title: Shared-memory IPC crates: shmem-ipc 0.3.0 last release 2022-11-22 (vendor 3x vs UDS at 64 KB); iceoryx2 0.10.0 (2026-09-18, Apache-2.0/MIT, Linux x86_64 tier 2) claims ~100 ns polling hops for 8 B offsets - both vendor numbers
summary: shmem-ipc (diwic): README "for a 64K packet, sharedring is three times faster than unix sockets", memfd sealing + eventfd signalling, dual Apache-2.0/MIT, 29 commits, no GitHub releases; my own memfd+futex ring measured 64KB echo 7.4 us vs 19.6 us UDS-raw = 2.6x, consistent. Independent M4 (non-Linux) re-bench found tuned UDS within 1-11% of shm (secondary, D). iceoryx2: repo reports charts only (i7-13700H, Linux 6.10.10, rustc 1.81.0); maintainer forum claim ~100 ns polling-mode for 8 B payload; Linux x86_64 tier 2 target tier 1; 225 open issues. Agnocast (arXiv 2506.16882) shows constant latency vs size for zero-copy static types. Decision: a hand-rolled ring is ~12 unsafe sites in my harness; a dependency adds a large unsafe TCB; UDS needs zero unsafe.
specifics: My harness shm path: 1 mmap + futex syscall + raw pointer slot access.

title: Precedents for moving code back in-process to cut IPC: Mozilla bug 864180 (audio codecs back into app process); GitHub Copilot runtime moved from a Node child process (~100 MB baseline) to an in-process cdylib
summary: Mozilla bugzilla 864180: codecs had been moved to a separate mediaserver process which added IPC overhead; fix loads software audio codecs in the application process. Copilot runtime rewrite (secondary write-ups): every SDK consumer spawned a Node.js child (~100 MB baseline, IPC latency, supervision) replaced by runtime.node loaded in-process via C ABI. Counterpoint (LWN thread on Rust in Chromium): memory-safe language and process isolation are complementary, not substitutes.
overclaim_risk: Secondary summaries; motive was resource footprint and packaging, not security.

title: UPDATE to ingress verdict: the single normalization core is justified by TCB/binary-size and by zero-copy Bytes (0 userspace copies, 30 us user CPU per 10 MB request), not by a large CPU win; the copy saving is 22% wall at 1 core and vanishes for small requests
summary: Direct measurement now backs the indirect evidence: Pingora ProxyHttp (pingora-proxy 0.9.0) already hands filters Option<Bytes> per chunk (not whole body), hyper/http-body 1.1.0 use Buf/Bytes frames; Bytes slice/clone are O(1) refcounts (bytes 1.12.1). A per-protocol owned-decode codec at 2-3 copies costs +0.58-0.72 ms per 10 MB (24-29 us/MB per copy). Claim retained: front ends must emit Bytes into one http::Request<Body>; claim dropped: any performance justification beyond large bodies.
overclaim_risk: Does not show per-protocol stacks are slower in practice; only that copies cost ~30 us/MB.

title: L5 harness spec: ipcbench (single binary, subcommands run|rss|norm), 1 pinned CPU, n>=10, no-op control, acceptance numbers per transport
summary: Spec: crate ipcbench (tokio 1, bytes 1, http 1, postcard 1.1.3 default-features=false, serde_bytes 0.11, libc 0.2, sha2 0.10, hmac 0.12; bincode only as control). Modes: `ipcbench run N` (transports inproc-dyn, uds-postcard, uds-bincode, uds-rawframe, tcp-loopback-rawframe, shm-futex, shm-spin5k; ops noop, echo64/4096/65536, redis_get, s3_presign; 300 warmup, 10-20k calls, per-call Instant latency, JSONL with p50/p90/p99/max/mean/calls_per_s/loadavg/cpus_allowed/cpuset/governor); `ipcbench rss` (exec vs fork-from-zygote 1/8/64 MB heap, n=1/8/32 children, /proc/pid/smaps_rollup Rss/Pss/Private_Dirty, spawn-to-first-reply n=200); `ipcbench norm N` (memcpy control, A/B1/B2 memory-only and socket pipelines, counting allocator pass separate from timed pass, getrusage user/sys). Commands: `HEAVY: tools/heavy.sh cargo build --release --offline` (CARGO_TARGET_DIR=state/raw/round-002/07-bench/target), then `taskset -c <idle cpu> target/release/ipcbench run 10 > ipc.jsonl`; control run with `taskset -c a,b` (2 CPUs). CI gate (acceptance criteria on the target VPS): noop UDS hop p50 <= 15 us and p99 <= 40 us; uds-raw 64KB echo <= 60 us; zero-copy path alloc bytes < 1% of body size and user CPU <= 100 us/10 MB; any regression >25% vs recorded baseline fails. Do not run spin variants on 1 vCPU (638 us/call). Files: state/raw/round-003/02-bench/{Cargo.toml,src/{main,rss,norm}.rs}.
specifics: Implementation-phase spike S1 (VPS): run the exact three commands on a 1-vCPU KVM $5 instance (not idle-guaranteed SMT) and record kernel, steal time from /proc/stat, loadavg; S2: add pipelined depth-16 UDS and a splice/sendfile variant of norm; S3: real redis 7/8 over loopback and MinIO/S3 presign with real driver crates (redis-rs/fred, aws-sigv4) to replace shaped ops; S4: rkyv 0.8.18 wire (not in offline cache here).

title: L5 decision table: adapter goes out-of-process when it has any C/C++ client, >15 unsafe sites, or is third-party AND its hop budget (rate x 4.8 us) fits; stays in-process when it is hot-path (>50k calls/s/core or op < 10 us) and pure Rust; reversal conditions stated
summary: Table (1 core, UDS+postcard/raw hop ~4.8 us p50, ~5.7 us p99; shm-futex ~2.1 us): (R1) C/C++ client library OR unsafe sites > ~15 at HEAD OR third-party/unreviewed OR driver memory-safety advisory in last 12 months => OUT of process (separate binary, seccomp+Landlock, UDS), provided hop share <= 10% of core: calls/s/core <= 20,000 (<= 2 hops per request => <= 10,000 rps). (R2) Same triggers but expected rate 20k-100k calls/s => stay out-of-process only with batching/pipelining (amortise to <= 1 us/op; spike S2) else the adapter C code must be replaced or the feature dropped from the default build; never move C into the front binary just for speed. (R3) pure Rust, <= 15 unsafe, first-party golden, op < 10 us or rate > 50k/s (token check, route lookup, header policy, SigV4 presign at 1.3 us) => IN process; hop would be 5.2x for presign and 100x for key lookups. (R4) pure Rust, ops 10-100 us (real redis/Scylla driver ops on loopback ~tens of us, unmeasured) => in-process by default; out-of-process allowed when the op is >= 50 us (hop <= 10%) and any trigger from R1 holds. (R5) Heavy compiler-bearing modules (wasmtime/Cranelift) => out of process or per-request wasm in-process only with pooled instances (r2: 20 us fresh instance, 52 KB) - unchanged. Reversal conditions (move OUT -> IN): measured hop p99 on target VPS > 40 us or hop share > 15% of core at observed p95 load; the C dependency is replaced by a pure-Rust fuzzed driver with <= 15 unsafe sites; or crash isolation is demonstrated unnecessary (no panic/abort path in 12 months of fuzzing). Reversal (IN -> OUT): unsafe count > 15, any C binding added, new memory-safety RUSTSEC/GHSA in the driver, or fuzz crash class not catchable by catch_unwind. Memory budget: each extra exec helper ~0.5 MB private + ~0.6 MB PSS minimal (real helper larger, spike S1); budget 8 helpers <= 40 MB on a 1 GB box.
specifics: Thresholds 15 unsafe sites, 10% core budget and 20k calls/s are policy choices derived from the measured 4.8 us hop and a 10% overhead budget, not from a controlled security study. Inputs: w02.ipc-hop-cost-1core, w02.redis-presign-shaped-ops, w02.helper-process-rss-spawn, dpf-l5-adapter-isolation.
overclaim_risk: Single-machine measurements; no real driver costs; 15-site cutoff inherited, not re-derived.
underclaim_risk: If hop is pipelined, rates well above 20k/s are feasible out-of-process.

title: L5 amendment to w02.L5-feature-gate-rule: add rules 5-8 (declared hop budget, wire format, serde_bytes, no spin on <=2 CPUs, CI perf gates)
summary: Append to the rule: (5) every out-of-process module declares op_cost_us and max_calls_per_s in its manifest; build fails if max_calls_per_s * 4.8 us > 10% of one core (CI computes from ipcbench baseline JSON). (6) Control-plane wire format is postcard 1.1.3 (no_std, maintained) or raw length-prefixed frames; bincode is forbidden (RUSTSEC-2025-0141); every byte-slice field uses serde_bytes (CI test: 64 KB echo over the UDS test transport <= 25 us on reference runner, else fail - catches the 4.9x pitfall). (7) Bodies never cross the module boundary inside the serialized message; pass body via fd/shared memfd or stream frames; headers/metadata only in postcard. (8) Shared-memory rings are not in the default build (unsafe TCB; UDS gives 4.8 us with zero unsafe); spin-waiting is forbidden when available_parallelism() <= 2 (638 us/call measured) - futex or eventfd only. (9) Ingress front ends must pass Bytes through without owned copies: CI test streams 10 MB through the normalization core and asserts allocator bytes < 1% of body and 0 explicit copies. Existing rules (1)-(4) unchanged.
specifics: Depends on w02.ipc-hop-cost-1core, w02.serde-bytes-pitfall, w02.bincode-unmaintained-use-postcard, w02.norm-copy-cost-measured.
overclaim_risk: The 25 us and 10% gate values are chosen with margin from laptop data and must be re-baselined on the target VPS (spike S1).
